clue.text: Electrical connector, one that may produce tear and cut

parts.note: a crocodile is fabled to weep false tears, hence 'crocodile tears'
to clip is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: An electrical part that somehow makes things rip and sever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' tempts as a rip, but it is a teardrop: crocodile tears are fake ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring clip with toothed jaws used to make a temporary electrical connection.

clue.text: Happened by chance to see royal court

parts.note: came can mean happened, as in 'it came about'
lot means chance or fate

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled by luck on a king's palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary seat of King Arthur and his knights.

clue.text: Like freemen, reduce allegiance to monarch?

parts.note: to own is to acknowledge, to profess allegiance to
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch
less, as in to make less, stands for reduce

explanation.surface: A question of whether free citizens owe less loyalty to the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the middle as an instruction: profess allegiance (OWN) to the monarch (ER) less, which is how free men stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Free men belong to no master, so they have nobody possessing them.

clue.text: Valuable sources in which Grimm originally found fairytale characters

indicators.note: 'in which' puts what follows inside the sources

parts.note: ores are the rocks from which valuable metals come

indicators.note: 'originally' asks for the first letter of the name Grimm

explanation.surface: The rich well where the Grimm brothers first discovered their storybook figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folk tales.

clue.text: Troublemaker's one exemption from punishment

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little troublemaker
unity is oneness, the number one

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker gets off scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Impunity is freedom from penalty or consequences.

clue.text: Product of terrible regime?

indicators.note: 'terrible' says the word regime is wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone created by an awful government.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a harsh regime drives people into exile.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is someone who has left their country, often fleeing political oppression.

clue.text: Engage in fight to secure some brass

parts.note: to lock is to secure
horns are among the brass instruments

explanation.surface: Brawling over guarding the band's trumpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Stags fight by entangling antlers, so the phrase means to clash.

clue.text: Putting a little money on, fascinated by horse

parts.note: P, a penny, is a small coin
into means keen on, as in 'into jazz'

explanation.surface: A gambler having a small bet, captivated by a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting ... on' places the coin in front of the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse.

clue.text: Ring again to cancel

definitions.meaning: ... means to sound bells once more
to annul or revoke a law

explanation.surface: Phone back to call something off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts as a phone call but means pealing bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Repealing a law revokes it; re-pealing bells sounds them again.

clue.text: What concentrates the mind poacher's first hazard when trespassing

parts.note: a mantra is a phrase repeated to focus the mind in meditation

indicators.note: 'first' asks for only the opening letter of the word poacher's

explanation.surface: A warning to poachers that something will sharpen their thinking if they wander onto private land.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap set on private land to catch intruders, so a danger to anyone trespassing.

clue.text: Outrage popular opinion when speaking

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: 'when speaking' says the word for opinion is heard rather than spelt, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: sense can mean a view or opinion, as in 'the sense of the meeting'

explanation.surface: Public views when voiced cause fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them furious, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fun and games producing exaltation

definitions.meaning: an exaltation is the collective noun for a flock of these songbirds, so they make one up

explanation.surface: Merriment that leads to rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exaltation' looks like joy, but it is the old collective noun for a group of larks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pranks are frivolous fun; the songbirds gather in a flock called an exaltation.

clue.text: Direction stick follows-that was Pooh's discovery

indicators.note: 'follows' places the word for stick after the word for direction

parts.note: north is a compass direction
a pole is a long stick

explanation.surface: A direction and a stick together lead to a famous bear's find.
explanation.walkthrough: In A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh, Pooh finds a pole on an expedition and it is proclaimed the great discovery of the polar destination.
explanation.definitionFit: In Milne's story Pooh's expedition ends when he finds a stick, which Christopher Robin names as the polar goal.

clue.text: Century of culture covering time new and old

parts.note: recent means new

explanation.surface: A cultured era spanning both modern and ancient times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' is just a link: the century takes in these pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian name for the 1300s, the fourteenth century, used of its art and literature.

clue.text: Mow rather roughly, chopping this?

indicators.note: 'roughly' says these letters are cut about into a new order

explanation.surface: Careless mowing might slice through a creature in the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing worm in garden soil, at risk from a mower blade.

clue.text: Crawl from wood to lake

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Creeping along from a forest down to the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawl' looks literal here but means to fawn abjectly.
explanation.definitionFit: To be servile and fawning, a figurative sense of crawling.

clue.text: Piece of music not paid for

definitions.meaning: an organ solo played before or after a church service

explanation.surface: A composition someone performed without a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpaid work is done freely; an organ voluntary is a solo piece.

clue.text: Bitter about the point coming from opposite direction

indicators.note: 'about' wraps the word for bitter round the following word

parts.note: sour means bitter
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Acid remarks about the tip of a weapon pointing the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite direction is relative to 12 across's northerly goal.
explanation.definitionFit: From the south, the reverse of the north named in a neighbouring clue.

clue.text: Extremely good person held church meeting

indicators.note: 'held' says the first word grips the second inside it

parts.note: very means extremely
ST, short for saint, is the crossword good person

explanation.surface: A thoroughly virtuous man hosted a parish gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is also a meeting of parishioners for church business, named after the room.

clue.text: Disparage biography omitting last year volume one should cover

indicators.note: in a down clue covering means sitting on top of the rest

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: 'omitting last' takes the final letter off the word for biography

parts.note: a life is a biography

explanation.surface: A hatchet-job memoir missing its final year, with a volume to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should cover' puts VI above the rest in this down entry; LIFE loses E to give LIF.
explanation.definitionFit: To vilify is to defame or speak ill of someone.

clue.text: Offered comfort when one's cold is bad

indicators.note: 'is bad' says the letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: the letters of one's, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone sympathised when a friend's chill was severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Consoled means comforted someone in distress, matching the past tense of offered comfort.

clue.text: Poet's written about the old lady deserving respect

indicators.note: 'written about' wraps the poet's name round an old word

parts.note: John Donne is the poet
ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: A poet wrote about an elderly woman worthy of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected senior woman in a field.

clue.text: Said peer so likely to be last in line?

definitions.text: so likely to be last in line?

indicators.note: 'Said' says the word for peer is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a baron is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A nobleman reportedly likely to end his family line.
explanation.walkthrough: Childless, a barren person has no heirs, so ends the line: fitting for a title-holding peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being infertile means having no descendants to continue a family.

clue.text: How casts become musical, and are daunted

definitions.meaning: remove the central letter of casts and you get the musical Cats
to be daunted is to become discouraged

explanation.surface: Theatre companies turning to song-and-dance shows and losing their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as an instruction: casts losing their middle S leaves CATS, the Lloyd Webber musical.
explanation.definitionFit: To become discouraged is to have one's courage fail, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Stick man

explanation.surface: A stick figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a walking stick; to staff is to supply with personnel.

clue.text: What's extremely chewy, sweet stuff?

parts.note: the outermost letters of chewy are a C with a Y, read out as two letters joined by a conjunction

explanation.surface: Something very chewy and sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: Name the first and last letters of 'chewy' as a pair, C with the joining word and then Y, and the phrase spells the sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for sweets, sugary confectionery.

clue.text: Shrub one may playfully cut

definitions.meaning: a Mediterranean bush whose flower buds are pickled
one cuts a skittish leap in the idiom 'cut a ...'

explanation.surface: A bush that someone prunes for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like pruning, but the idiom is to cut a frisky leap.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush yields pickled buds; a frolicsome jump is one you cut.

clue.text: Relish money given in support

indicators.note: 'given in' puts the letter for money inside the word for support

parts.note: favour means support or backing
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Enjoy cash handed over as backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a verb, enjoy, but it is the noun for taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish can mean a distinctive taste or savour.

clue.text: Justify one-time scheme I concealed

parts.note: ex means former, one-time

indicators.note: 'concealed' says the letter I is tucked away inside the word for scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: Someone defends a past plot they kept hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for or give reasons for something, a synonym of justify.

clue.text: How poet might describe shady lady?

definitions.text: How poet might describe shady lady?

parts.words: How poet might describe shady lady?
parts.note: read not as a disreputable woman but as the words shady and lady, a two-syllable rhyme ending on an unstressed syllable

explanation.surface: A poet describing a woman of dubious morals.
explanation.walkthrough: A rhyme whose stress falls on the penultimate syllable, like shady/lady, has a gendered technical name.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosody's term for a rhyme of a stressed then unstressed syllable, such as shady with lady.
